result:
If I could snap my fingers and change one thing, I'd make relentless curiosity the default setting for every human mind.

Not "be nicer" or "share more" or some other vague platitude. Just a built-in, unignorable drive to figure out how the universe actually works, even when the answer is uncomfortable, expensive, or politically inconvenient. Most of our biggest problems—poverty, disease, conflict, stagnation—aren't mysteries of physics. They're failures of understanding, coordination, and incentives. Fix the curiosity deficit and the rest starts compounding in the right direction: better science, better energy, better institutions, longer lives, and eventually a species that can actually leave this rock if it needs to.

Everything else is downstream of that.
